confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from crowd-sourced averages (MyLifeElsewhere, Expatistan) with small samples, converted from MXN at roughly 17.5 MXN per USD. Restaurant beer, cappuccino and inexpensive-meal figures are the most reliable. The mid-range two-person meal is derived from an Expatistan dinner-for-two figure that included wine, so I reduced it to an estimate without drinks. Cocktail and wine are weaker: the only cocktail data point is one downtown club price (about MX$267), so the cocktail anchor is set from the local beer relationship (roughly 2.5 to 3 times the beer price) rather than direct evidence. Wine uses the same beer-relationship basis. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July high season from general knowledge and the city context; no accommodation prices were searched or live listings inspected, so they are the least certain. FX caveat: the RBA exchange-rates page surfaced in search, and its most recent observation I could verify was 0.7088 USD per AUD on 2026-03-20. I could not confirm a more recent RBA observation within the search budget, so this rate is about seven months older than the generation date and should be refreshed before use. Third-party sites showed different late-2026 rates, which I did not use because they are not RBA data.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mexican Caribbean resort-town pricing, with the tourist-zone premium over interior Mexican cities. Food and drink are based on MyLifeElsewhere and Expatistan user-submitted averages for Playa del Carmen. Accommodation is a holistic model estimate for July high season, informed by typical Riviera Maya resort-town rate levels, not by any searched listings.
